messages.content:
You are reviewing one authorized localhost-only TRACE-WAF training lab.
Propose ONE conservative JSON rule policy; no shell commands, raw ModSecurity directives or control of deployment.
The schema MUST be exactly {"exempt_routes": ["/docs","/search"], "patterns": [{"route":"/sql","regex":"..."}, {"route":"/xss","regex":"..."}, {"route":"/file","regex":"..."}], "rationale":"...", "risks":"..."}.
Route semantics: /sql is a deliberately vulnerable SQLite concat query, /xss renders an unsafe HTML fragment, /file reads a synthetic canary if traversal is effective; /docs and /search HTML-escape q. A policy must preserve benign functionality and avoid false positives, not merely block more attacks. Report risks of regex on SQL comments and legitimate strings. Only dev-side observations are supplied: CRS stock FP is high, a fixed non-LLM route-level adjustment helps but benign false positives persist. Heuristic control and all LLM proposals must be tested at the same CRS paranoia level. Restrict to 2 route exemptions and at most 3 regex patterns each <=512 chars, compiled by a separate restricted compiler. DO NOT change anomaly threshold or disable WAF globally. The /sql regex must NOT reject standalone punctuation `--` in a benign string. The /file rules must distinguish permissible public-readme paths from traversal to the synthetic secret. Do not mention any held-out test cases or their results. Return the JSON object only.

message.content: {"exempt_routes":["/docs","/search"],"patterns":[{"route":"/sql","regex":"(?i)\\bunion\\s+(?:all\\s+)?select\\b|(?:^|[\\s'\"])\\b(?:or|and)\\s+(?:\\d+\\s*=\\s*\\d+|'[^'\\r\\n]{0,64}'\\s*=\\s*'[^'\\r\\n]{0,64}')"},{"route":"/xss","regex":"(?i)<\\s*script\\b|<[^>\\r\\n]{0,200}\\s+on[a-z]{3,24}\\s*=|javascript\\s*:|data\\s*:\\s*text/html"},{"route":"/file","regex":"(?i)(?:\\.|%2e|%252e){2}(?:/|\\\\|%2f|%5c|%252f|%255c)"}],"rationale":"Exempt only the two documented HTML-escaping routes. Apply narrow, route-specific checks elsewhere: SQL UNION and tautology structures without treating standalone -- punctuation as malicious; executable HTML markers on the unsafe fragment route; and dot-dot path components, including common encoded forms, on the file route. Ordinary public-readme paths remain permissible. Evaluate this policy, heuristic control, and all LLM proposals at the same CRS paranoia level.","risks":"Regex cannot fully parse SQL, HTML, URL decoding, or normalization. SQL comments can split tokens and evade structural matching, while broader comment rules would falsely reject legitimate strings containing -- or comment-like text. Legitimate prose, code examples, event-handler documentation, javascript: text, or paths intentionally containing parent-directory components may still trigger. Alternate encodings, malformed markup, unusual SQLite syntax, double decoding beyond covered forms, absolute paths, symlink behavior, and platform-specific separators may bypass these patterns; the separate restricted compiler must verify supported syntax and matching semantics."}
